source: Lencioni T, Carpinella I, Rabuffetti M, Marzegan A, Ferrarin M (2019). Human kinematic, kinetic and EMG data during different walking and stair ascending and descending tasks. Scientific Data 6:309. doi:10.1038/s41597-019-0323-z
angle_convention_note: Sagittal ankle angle (AnkleFlx), dorsiflexion positive (per dataset's walking_fig.m plot title 'Ankle Dorsiflexion Angle'). Referenced to each subject's quiet-standing posture by subtracting StandingData.Ang[AnkleFlx] (the raw dataset uses a marker-based convention with a subject-specific offset, standing ankle angle typically ~-10..-15 deg raw; the dataset provides the standing trial for offset removal).
moment_convention_note: Sagittal ankle moment (AnkleFlxMom) exactly as stored: already normalized by body mass (N.m/kg, per walking_fig.m title 'Ankle Moment (Nm/kg)'); plantarflexor (internal extensor) moment positive - verified by classic shape: single positive peak in late stance (~45-50% cycle), small negative dorsiflexor moment after heel strike.
extraction_note: Per subject: Task=='Walking' trials cluster into 3 speed blocks (protocol: 5 natural + 5 progressively faster + 5 progressively slower trials); 1-D 3-means clustering on trial speed, middle cluster taken as natural/self-selected. Trials with NaNs dropped. Trial curves (already time-normalized to 101 points, 0-100% gait cycle, both feet pooled) averaged within subject, then unweighted mean across 48 subjects (ages 6-72, dataset spans 6-72 y). Skipped: ['Subject29.mat (empty natural cluster)', 'Subject36.mat (too few walking trials)']. Extracted with scipy.io from per-subject .mat files (fields s.Data[i].Ang/Mom rows AnkleFlx/AnkleFlxMom).
